headline: PM Tarique Rahman discusses Rohingya crisis, climate change with UN chief
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres at the UN headquarters to find sustainable solutions for the Rohingya crisis and combat climate change.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres met on Thursday at the UN headquarters in New York to discuss the Rohingya crisis and climate change.
The meeting took place on the 27th floor of the UN Secretariat Building during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
The two leaders exchanged views on Bangladesh's development journey and the country's continued contribution to UN peace, security, and development efforts.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman highlighted the importance of UN cooperation and support for Bangladesh's national interests and priorities.
Tarique Rahman also reiterated Bangladesh's commitment to multilateralism, international cooperation, peace, and sustainable development.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stressed the importance of advancing the longstanding cooperation between Bangladesh and the UN.
Both leaders expressed their resolve to continue working closely together to address common global challenges.
caption:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and UN chief Antonio Guterres meet in New York to tackle the Rohingya crisis and climate change.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres met on Thursday at the UN headquarters in New York to discuss the Rohingya crisis and climate change.

The meeting took place on the 27th floor of the UN Secretariat Building during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The two leaders exchanged views on Bangladesh's development journey and the country's continued contribution to UN peace, security, and development efforts.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman highlighted the importance of UN cooperation and support for Bangladesh's national interests and priorities.

Tarique Rahman also reiterated Bangladesh's commitment to multilateralism, international cooperation, peace, and sustainable development.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stressed the importance of advancing the longstanding cooperation between Bangladesh and the UN.

Both leaders expressed their resolve to continue working closely together to address common global challenges.

headline: Dozens of envoys walk out of Netanyahu's UN speech in protest
summary: Delegates jeered and booed the Israeli Prime Minister as he addressed the General Assembly, while the Palestinian delegation coordinated the protest.
details: Dozens of envoys from across the world walked out of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech to the UN on Thursday.
The walkout was a coordinated protest against the Israeli leader, with the Palestinian delegation having called for other missions to join them in a memo.
As Netanyahu began his address, delegates jeered and booed, prompting the session speaker to shout for order.
In a defiant response, Netanyahu told those remaining in the hall, "If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left this hall, please do so now."
The hall, which was sparsely filled earlier in the session, had gradually filled up just before the speech began.
caption:
Dozens of global envoys walked out of the UN in protest as Benjamin Netanyahu began his speech.

Dozens of envoys from across the world walked out of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech to the UN on Thursday.

The walkout was a coordinated protest against the Israeli leader, with the Palestinian delegation having called for other missions to join them in a memo.

As Netanyahu began his address, delegates jeered and booed, prompting the session speaker to shout for order.

In a defiant response, Netanyahu told those remaining in the hall, "If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left this hall, please do so now."

The hall, which was sparsely filled earlier in the session, had gradually filled up just before the speech began.
